paper_title: Knowing You Don't Know Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round   RAG through Self-Practicing
caption: Ablation study on different Critic model choices. Both follow the SIM-RAG setting with GPT-4 as the Reasoner, but the blue bar uses learned Flan-T5-783M as a Critic, while the red bar uses GPT-4 as the Critic (a.k.a., self-critique).
model_annotation: The bar chart presents an ablation study comparing two different Critic models—Flan-T5-783M (blue bars) and GPT-4 (red bars)—within the SIM-RAG framework, where GPT-4 serves as the Reasoner in both cases. The horizontal axis lists six evaluation metrics across three datasets: TriviaQA, HotPotQA, and 2Wiki, each assessed under two metrics: Exact Match (EM) and F1 score. The vertical axis represents performance scores on a linear scale ranging from 25 to 85, with tick marks at intervals of 20. For each dataset-metric pair, two adjacent bars are shown, with the blue bar representing the Flan-T5-783M Critic and the red bar representing the GPT-4 Critic. The scores are labeled directly on top of each bar. In TriviaQA (EM), Flan-T5-783M scores 77.3 and GPT-4 scores 77.1; in HotPotQA (EM), Flan-T5-783M scores 37.0 and GPT-4 scores 31.9; in 2Wiki (EM), Flan-T5-783M scores 44.5 and GPT-4 scores 32.5. In TriviaQA (F1), Flan-T5-783M scores 82.8 and GPT-4 scores 83.8; in HotPotQA (F1), Flan-T5-783M scores 49.7 and GPT-4 scores 43.3; in 2Wiki (F1), Flan-T5-783M scores 53.3 and GPT-4 scores 38.1. The bars are arranged in groups by dataset and metric, with the blue bar consistently appearing to the left of the red bar within each group. The chart visually indicates that Flan-T5-783M performs comparably or slightly better than GPT-4 in most cases, except for TriviaQA (F1), where GPT-4 slightly outperforms. The bars are not sorted by height but by the dataset-metric categories, and no visual emphasis (such as shading or outlines) is applied to any specific bar.
